title: Peak-Set Enrichment Analysis with PeakSEA
text: Peak-Set Enrichment Analysis (PeakSEA) computational method identifying peak sets — collections genomic regions sharing biological property — -represented among peaks differentially regulated conditions. PeakSEA adapts Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) framework (Subramanian et al., 2005) genomic ranges data. key conceptual differences : approach can example applied chromatin accessibility experiments one wishes ask: “peaks near binding sites TF X tend open condition ?”

Overlap peaks with peak sets         ▼   Annotate each peak with the term(s) it overlaps         │         │  2. Build ranked gene-set input for GSEA         ▼   TERM2GENE data frame  +  named ranked vector         │         │  3. Run GSEA (clusterProfiler)         ▼   gseaResult: NES, p-value, FDR per peak set

title: Peak-Set Enrichment Analysis with PeakSEA
text: gr must GRanges object whose metadata contains quantitative ranking metric. Common choices: log2FC differential accessibility test (e.g. DESeq2, edgeR) Signed −log⁡10(p-value)-\log_{10}(p\text{-value}) continuous score larger values indicate stronger signal condition interest
code: library(PeakSEA) library(plyranges)  set.seed(1979)  # 100 simulated ATAC-seq peaks with strong signal: #   peaks 1–50 are upregulated (positive log2FC) #   peaks 51–100 are downregulated (negative log2FC) peaks <- data.frame(   seqnames = "chr1",   start    = seq(1e4, by = 1e3, length.out = 100),   width    = 500L,   log2FC   = c(seq(5, 0.1, length.out = 50),                seq(-0.1, -5, length.out = 50)),   padj     = runif(100, 0, 0.05) ) |>   plyranges::as_granges()  peaks #> GRanges object with 100 ranges and 2 metadata columns: #>         seqnames        ranges strand |    log2FC       padj #>            <Rle>     <IRanges>  <Rle> | <numeric>  <numeric> #>     [1]     chr1   10000-10499      * |       5.0 0.04544498 #>     [2]     chr1   11000-11499      * |       4.9 0.02410026 #>     [3]     chr1   12000-12499      * |       4.8 0.01264799 #>     [4]     chr1   13000-13499      * |       4.7 0.03642297 #>     [5]     chr1   14000-14499      * |       4.6 0.00827964 #>     ...      ...           ...    ... .       ...        ... #>    [96]     chr1 105000-105499      * |      -4.6  0.0119499 #>    [97]     chr1 106000-106499      * |      -4.7  0.0375665 #>    [98]     chr1 107000-107499      * |      -4.8  0.0201940 #>    [99]     chr1 108000-108499      * |      -4.9  0.0232156 #>   [100]     chr1 109000-109499      * |      -5.0  0.0108765 #>   ------- #>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths

title: Peak-Set Enrichment Analysis with PeakSEA
text: gr_set GRanges object every range annotated "term" metadata column naming peak set belongs . mirrors TERM2GENE format used clusterProfiler. Peak sets can represent, example: TF binding sites ChIP-seq experiments (ENCODE, ReMap) Chromatin states histone mark ChIP-seq (Roadmap Epigenomics) DHS clusters DNase-seq custom collection genomic intervals Public databases LOLA AnnotationHub provide pre-built region sets can used directly gr_set. vignette create two synthetic peak sets mimic TF binding sites overlapping known subset differential peaks:
code: # "TF_A" binding sites overlap the upregulated peaks # "TF_B" binding sites overlap the downregulated peaks set.seed(1979) peak_sets <- c(   shift_right(peaks[sample(1:60, 40)],  100L) |> mutate(term = "TF_A"),   shift_right(peaks[sample(40:100, 40)], 100L) |> mutate(term = "TF_B") )  peak_sets #> GRanges object with 80 ranges and 3 metadata columns: #>        seqnames      ranges strand |    log2FC      padj        term #>           <Rle>   <IRanges>  <Rle> | <numeric> <numeric> <character> #>    [1]     chr1 55100-55599      * |       0.5 0.0270753        TF_A #>    [2]     chr1 46100-46599      * |       1.4 0.0462161        TF_A #>    [3]     chr1 11100-11599      * |       4.9 0.0241003        TF_A #>    [4]     chr1 68100-68599      * |      -0.9 0.0210772        TF_A #>    [5]     chr1 41100-41599      * |       1.9 0.0348013        TF_A #>    ...      ...         ...    ... .       ...       ...         ... #>   [76]     chr1 56100-56599      * |       0.4 0.0308319        TF_B #>   [77]     chr1 60100-60599      * |      -0.1 0.0212098        TF_B #>   [78]     chr1 50100-50599      * |       1.0 0.0279952        TF_B #>   [79]     chr1 69100-69599      * |      -1.0 0.0120466        TF_B #>   [80]     chr1 98100-98599      * |      -3.9 0.0105650        TF_B #>   ------- #>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths

title: Peak-Set Enrichment Analysis with PeakSEA
text: Call psea() ranked peaks, name ranking column, peak set database. Additional arguments forwarded plyranges::join_overlap_left() (e.g. maxgap, minoverlap) control overlaps gr gr_set computed. result gseaResult object. embedded result table can accessed data frame: Interpreting output: NES > 0: peak set enriched among upregulated peaks (top ranked list). NES < 0: peak set enriched among downregulated peaks (bottom ranked list). p.adjust: FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg default). expected, TF_A (associated upregulated peaks) positive NES, TF_B (associated downregulated peaks) negative NES.

title: Peak-Set Enrichment Analysis with PeakSEA
text: real analysis, gr_set typically built external database. minimal sketch using AnnotationHub: collections many peak sets, concatenate individual GRanges objects c() passing psea().
code: library(AnnotationHub) ah <- AnnotationHub()  # Search for ENCODE CTCF ChIP-seq peaks in hg38 ctcf_hits <- query(ah, c("CTCF", "Homo sapiens", "ENCODE"))  # Download Gm12878 cell line data ctcf_gr <- ah[["AH22521"]]  # Annotate with a term column and combine multiple experiments ctcf_gr$term <- "CTCF_ENCODE"  # Pass as gr_set result <- psea(my_atac_peaks, log2FC, ctcf_gr)

title: Peak-set enrichment analysis
text: goal PeakSEA test enrichment public peak set data using preranked peak data input. NB: renamed package PSEA PeakSEA avoid confusion packages. example ATACseq peak can tested DiffBind differential opening, ranking metrics, log Fold change can used. can test enrichment opening () closing () publicly available databases, eg LOLAcore epigenetic annotations causalDB finemapped credible intervals disease loci derived GWAS dataset. PSEA returns gseResult object compatible DOSE package routines.

title: Peak-Set Enrichment Analysis (PSEA) — psea
text: gr GRanges object peak ranking metric metadata columns. rank_col Bare column name gr metadata use ranking peaks. gr_set GRanges object annotating peak set membership. Must contain metadata column named "term" labels range peak set identifier. ... Additional arguments passed plyranges::join_overlap_left() (e.g. maxgap, minoverlap).
